newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Lee to receive democracy award in U.S..
newsitem.headline: HK's Lee to receive democracy award in U.S..

text.p: The leader of Hong Kong's Democratic Party, Martin Lee, will go to the United States next month to collect an award for championing democracy in the British colony, which reverts Chinese rule this July.
Lee said in a statement on Monday he would attend a reception on Washington's Capitol Hill on April 9 to accept the National Endowment for Democracy's 1997 Democracy Award.
"This is a great honour, which reflects the efforts of all Hong Kong people to preserve freedom and democracy in our home," he said.
Previous winners of the award include Czechoslavak dissident-turned-president Vaclav Havel.
Hong Kong, a free-wheeling British colony for more than 150 years, is to be handed back to communist China at midnight on June 30.
The territory of 6.4 million has been promised considerable autonomy and that its capitalist way of life will remain unchanged for 50 years after the handover.
But Beijing's avowed plans to cut civil liberties and replace the elected legislature, in which Lee's democrats are the largest single party, have raised doubts whether China will keep its word.
Lee has been a vocal opponent of Beijing's plans.
